**My pick: BLUETTI AC200L — the best overall choice for RV boondocking under $1,000.**

Based on the supplied search results, it offers an unusually good combination of battery capacity, inverter power, and RV-specific connectivity.

<row align=start gap={3}>
  <AsyncImage query="BLUETTI AC200L portable power station front view" aspectRatio="3:4" maxWidth="116px"/>
  <box flex="1" gap={1}>
    **<Entity category="product" value="BLUETTI AC200L" disambig="2048Wh LiFePO4 portable power station"/>**
    <title color="success" size="2xl" tabularNums={true}>$854.05</title>
    <text color="secondary" size="xs">With code AFF5OFF · Listed price $899</text>
    - 2,048Wh LiFePO4 battery
    - 2,400W continuous AC output
    - 1,200W maximum solar input
    - Built-in 30A TT-30 RV outlet
    - Designed for RV integration
    <text color="secondary" size="xs">Source: Dealectric result, October 31, 2026.</text>
    [See deal at Dealectric](https://dealectric.com/go/bluetti-ac200l)
  </box>
</row>

### Why I recommend it

1. **RV-friendly connection:** Built-in TT-30 outlet means you don't need to rely on an ordinary household outlet adapter to connect to an RV.
2. **Good capacity:** 2,048Wh is enough for many essential RV loads during a day of boondocking.
3. **Strong inverter:** 2,400W can handle appliances such as a coffee maker, microwave (depending on wattage), refrigerator, and water pump.
4. **LiFePO4 chemistry:** Better long-term cycle life than conventional lithium-ion batteries.

### Other contenders

| Model | Capacity | Output | Price | Best for |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---|
| BLUETTI AC200L | 2,048Wh | 2,400W | $854 | RV integration |
| Jackery Explorer 2000 v2 | 2,042Wh | 2,200W | $999 | General RV use |
| EcoFlow DELTA 2 Max | 2,048Wh | — | $999 | Solar charging |
| Anker SOLIX C1000 Gen 2 | 1,024Wh | 2,000W | $699 | Lightweight RV trips |

### Important things to know

- The AC200L's TT-30 outlet provides approximately 20A of usable power, not the full 30A RV service.
- It is not intended to run a rooftop RV air conditioner continuously.
- If your RV has a two-way refrigerator, use propane rather than AC mode when boondocking to conserve battery.
- The AC200L is an older model, and its availability may change. The supplied results reported it in stock on October 31, 2026.

### Final verdict

<badge color="success">Best overall RV pick</badge>

I'd choose the **BLUETTI AC200L at approximately $854** over the Jackery Explorer 2000 v2 at $999 because the built-in TT-30 outlet makes it particularly suitable for RV use.

One important distinction: if you're planning extended boondocking with a residential refrigerator, microwave, and significant solar charging, I'd prioritize a 2kWh system rather than a 1kWh unit.
